clue.text: Recurrent trouble with crack in holy building

indicators.note: recurrent in its sense of running back towards its origin, so the two pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
a gap is a crack or opening

explanation.surface: A building of worship keeps suffering from a crack that comes back again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recurrent' turns ADO + GAP (ADOGAP) backwards as one run; it uses the anatomical sense of running back the way it came, as Chambers allows.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered tower serving as a Buddhist or Hindu temple, an example of a holy building.

clue.text: Extremely unhealthy-looking couples in history

indicators.note: in places the couples word inside the history word

parts.note: the past is history
ties are links or couplings

explanation.surface: Couples in history who looked thoroughly sickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasty means pale and unhealthy in complexion, and the superlative gives the extreme form.

clue.text: Work well together raising support

indicators.note: in a down clue raising means the word is read upwards

parts.note: a leg supports a table or chair

explanation.surface: Raising the backing a team needs helps it work well together.
explanation.definitionFit: To gel is to cohere, as a team does when its members combine effectively.

clue.text: In kitchen, cleaner finds one's husband in pain

indicators.note: the second in places one's and husband inside the pain word

parts.note: a drag, like a pain, is something tedious
one is I and the possessive gives S

explanation.surface: A kitchen cleaner discovers that her husband is in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleaner' looks like a person, but it is the cloth itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishrag is a cloth for washing dishes, a cleaner found in the kitchen.

clue.text: I get shot of something or someone fighting

definitions.meaning: one who scraps things, discarding or getting rid of them
a scrap is a fight, so one who scraps is a fighter

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of the verb scrap: to discard and to brawl, each with its agent noun.

clue.text: Meeting before match reportedly bearing fruit

indicators.note: before puts the meeting word ahead of the next piece

parts.note: a conference is a formal meeting

indicators.note: reportedly means a word that sounds like the synonym for match

parts.note: a pair is a match, two that go together

explanation.surface: A pre-game briefing that seems to be paying off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing fruit' reads as succeeding; 'fruit' alone is the definition, 'bearing' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Conference is a well-known English variety of pear, a long green fruit.

clue.text: Dope in military base behind enemy lines

definitions.meaning: a dope is a fool, an idiot
a forward area seized in enemy territory and held for landing troops and supplies by aircraft

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a brainless person, and the air-landing counterpart of a beachhead.

clue.text: Very quickly, Poles enlist God for battle

parts.note: presto is the musical direction for very fast

indicators.note: the poles enlist, taking in, the god between them

parts.note: N and S are the north and south poles
Pan is the Greek god of the wild

explanation.surface: In great haste, Polish soldiers sign up a deity for a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Poles is the compass points, not people from Poland. Prestonpans (1745) was a Jacobite victory near Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of Prestonpans was the first major clash of the 1745 Jacobite Rising.

clue.text: Enthusiastic, head over heels about good music

indicators.note: about means the turned word goes round the good letter
head over heels in a down clue means the word is turned upside down

parts.note: eager means enthusiastic

explanation.surface: Someone madly enthusiastic about good music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head over heels' turns EAGER into REGAE, then 'about' wraps it round G.
explanation.definitionFit: Reggae is a style of popular music that originated in Jamaica.

clue.text: Edited short article with headline Chap shooting back in Lancaster

indicators.note: edited text is rewritten, so these letters are rearranged
short means the article word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: An editor cuts a piece and gives it a headline about a gunman firing in Lancaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics suggest a newspaper headline; Lancaster is the RAF Second World War bomber, not the city, and its rear gunner was the tail-end Charlie.
explanation.definitionFit: RAF slang for the rear gunner in a bomber's tail turret, firing at attackers from behind.

clue.text: Novel involving Mars and aliens, ending in war

indicators.note: involving in its old sense of rolling up or entangling, so the letters are twisted together
the final letter of war is taken

explanation.surface: A science-fiction book in which Martians invade and the story closes with a war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' looks like the definition's link, but it shuffles MARS + ALIENS + R (the end of 'war', from 'ending in').
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot's 1861 book about a weaver of Raveloe is a classic Victorian novel.

clue.text: Say, good start in life

parts.note: e.g. (for example) is signalled by say

explanation.surface: A good beginning to someone's life, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Every bird begins its existence inside an egg, so it is literally where a life starts.

clue.text: Commanding, ignoring a risk

indicators.note: ignoring the word a means that letter is left out of the synonym

parts.note: imperial means commanding, majestic

explanation.surface: Someone in command who pays no attention to danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'risk' is a verb here: to imperil something is to put it at risk.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to expose something to danger or jeopardy.

clue.text: A petrol fire put out by snowball

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A fire started with petrol is extinguished by a snowball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snowball' is a verb: to grow rapidly.
explanation.definitionFit: To snowball is to grow or multiply rapidly, the same as increasing quickly in number.

clue.text: Return with fighting force for vengeful daughter

parts.note: to return a candidate is to elect them to Parliament
RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: A daughter comes home with an army to take her revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' is the British political sense: voters return an MP by electing them.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Agamemnon's daughter avenged her father's murder by driving her brother to kill their mother.

clue.text: Labour doesn't anticipate this quickly organised union meeting

definitions.text: Labour doesn't anticipate this quickly organised union meeting

parts.words: Labour doesn't anticipate this quickly organised union meeting
parts.note: labour is childbirth, which was not expected to come before this hastily arranged marriage ceremony

explanation.surface: The Labour Party is caught off guard by a hastily called trade union meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour and union pull towards British politics and trade unions; they are childbirth and marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding arranged in haste because the bride is pregnant, so the baby arrives within wedlock.

clue.text: Heretic from height thrown into river

indicators.note: thrown into puts the height inside the river

parts.note: the Wye is a river on the England-Wales border
a cliff is a height

explanation.surface: A heretic flung from a clifftop into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: John Wycliffe, the 14th-century English reformer, was condemned by the Church as a heretic.

clue.text: House for lending out in capital seen by visitors

indicators.note: seen by places the visitors word right beside the capital word

parts.note: capital is money, finance
guests in the house are company

explanation.surface: A home let out in a capital city, viewed by tourists.
explanation.definitionFit: A finance company is a firm whose business is advancing money as loans, a lending house.

clue.text: In local possibly take half hour over drink

indicators.note: take means the rearranged letters hold the other piece
possibly means the letters of local might be arranged differently
half means the first two of the four letters of hour

explanation.surface: In the pub you might spend half an hour over a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Local is the British word for one's neighbourhood pub; 'possibly' scrambles LOCAL to ALCOL, which takes in HO.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcohol is the general term for intoxicating drink.

clue.text: I run, given cover by fanatical soldiers in tower

indicators.note: given cover by means the fanatical word goes round I and run

parts.note: mad means fanatical, as in mad about
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Someone flees, sheltered by zealous troops in a tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirador is a turret or belvedere giving a view, a watchtower in Spanish architecture.

clue.text: Missing son kidnapped by a criminal

indicators.note: kidnapped by puts the son inside the criminal

parts.note: bent is slang for crooked or criminal

explanation.surface: A missing boy has been abducted by a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: Absent means not present, gone missing.

clue.text: Slav, heading west, spies Italian city

indicators.note: in an across clue heading west means read from right to left

parts.note: a Serb is a Slav
the CIA is the US spy agency

explanation.surface: A Slavic traveller going west catches sight of a town in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Brescia is a Lombardy city in northern Italy, between Milan and Verona.

clue.text: Reading material written about posh girl

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the fabric word is read backwards

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric
U means upper-class, posh
Sal is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A book has been written about a society girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reading material' looks like one phrase, but 'Reading' is the definition and 'material' is REP, a ribbed cloth; 'about' turns it to PER.
explanation.definitionFit: A perusal is a careful read-through of something, so the act of reading it.

clue.text: When to expect letter from abroad

definitions.meaning: the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation for estimated time of arrival, and also a Greek character.

clue.text: I'll make one a bevvy of mild with bitter

definitions.text: I'll make one a bevvy of mild with bitter

parts.words: I'll make one a bevvy of mild with bitter
parts.note: two halves add up to one whole, and the drink of that name mixes mild ale with bitter

explanation.surface: A barman offers to mix a pint of mild and bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: Bevvy is British slang for an alcoholic drink; mild and bitter are two styles of British beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Half plus half makes a whole, and the phrase is also a pub mix of two beers.

clue.text: Help girl men won't ring

indicators.note: the men no longer ring the girl's middle, so those outer letters are dropped

parts.note: a maiden is a girl
taken as written

explanation.surface: A helpful girl whom no man will phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like a phone call; it is the letters M and EN that surround AID in MAIDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Aid and help are synonyms, both meaning assistance.

clue.text: Gloom and doom for Chelsea?

definitions.meaning: a state of sadness and depression
Chelsea Football Club is nicknamed for its blue kit

explanation.definitionFit: A phrase for melancholy that is also the nickname of a London football club, Chelsea FC.

clue.text: Clear confusion about daughter's birthplace

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the daughter
confusion means the letters of clear are jumbled

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Sort out the muddle over where a daughter was born.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusion' scrambles CLEAR to CRALE; 'about' puts it round D.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a cradle is the place where something is born or nurtured, as in the cradle of civilisation.
